title: 48 rabies deaths by August: Vietnam needs stronger biosecurity
excerpt: Vietnam reported 48 rabies deaths by 21 August 2026. Household exposure and illicit dog-trade risks demand stronger quarantine, inspection, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
Forty-eight people had died from rabies across Vietnam by 21 August 2026, according to a report cited by Hải Phòng local authorities. Each death marks a preventable failure: exposure occurred, urgent care did not stop infection, and clinical disease became almost universally fatal.

Every missed exposure carries a human cost

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek urgent medical assessment for post-exposure prophylaxis: vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Treatment must begin before symptoms. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal.

These household exposure incidents must not be falsely presented as proof that any individual death came from commercial dog meat. They show one dimension of broken biosecurity. The dog trade presents another: uninspected slaughter, animal handling, and transport can move animals through communities outside reliable veterinary oversight.

Quarantine cannot stop at household gates

Local authorities are tightening controls. Đà Nẵng’s plan provides for holding roaming dogs and cats at a facility near km13 on the Nam Hải Vân bypass, with public notice and a stated 48-hour process for unclaimed animals. Owners also face duties to register animals, vaccinate against rabies, and prevent roaming.

Vietnamese families and local leaders should not have to defend homes, pets, and public health against illicit operators whose networks profit from stolen companions and weak inspection. Lawful ownership is not the target. Criminal theft, illegal transport, quarantine evasion, and unsafe slaughter demand enforcement.

Demand one clear national standard

Public health targets require more than vaccination campaigns. They require traceable transport, veterinary inspection, accountable holding facilities, and enforcement that reaches commercial pipelines. Stop Dog Eaters calls for complete nationwide abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, then follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
